current_row.boundary_rationale: Onset: the book opens on two datelines in two counting systems - בִּשְׁלֹשִׁ֣ים שָׁנָ֗ה (oshb:Ezek.1.1, a regnal/exilic year the book never names an era for) and הַשָּׁנָ֣ה הַחֲמִישִׁ֔ית לְגָל֖וּת הַמֶּ֥לֶךְ יוֹיָכִֽין (oshb:Ezek.1.2, the fifth year of Jehoiachin's exile) - followed at oshb:Ezek.1.3 by the superscription הָיֹ֣ה הָיָ֣ה דְבַר יְ֠הוָה אֶל יְחֶזְקֵ֨אל, an infinitive-absolute-plus-perfect word-event with a THIRD-PERSON addressee ('to Ezekiel', not 'to me'). This verb and addressee shape are why the verse sits in the 49-verse any-form word-event count and not the 48-verse first-person family (sweep: verses containing the word-event phrase in any form, 49; the 48 excludes this one verse by predicate). It is weighed here as a real onset in its own right, not folded into or discounted against the vision that follows. The same verse also carries וַתְּהִ֥י עָלָ֛יו שָׁ֖ם יַד יְהוָֽה, the hand-of-YHWH construct that opens the book's first vision (one of 7 verses carrying the construct). Close: the scene runs unbroken to oshb:Ezek.1.28, מַרְאֵ֖ה דְּמ֣וּת כְּבוֹד יְהוָ֑ה וָֽאֶרְאֶה֙ וָאֶפֹּ֣ל עַל פָּנַ֔י וָאֶשְׁמַ֖ע ק֥וֹל מְדַבֵּֽר, glossed by the WEB as “this was the appearance of the likeness of Yahweh's glory. When I saw it, I fell on my face, and I heard a voice of one that spoke” (web:Ezek.1.28). No word-event, messenger, recognition or utterance formula interrupts 1:4-1:27 (the transport-verb and 'he said to me' sweeps that mark scene changes elsewhere in the book's visions do not begin until chapter 8), so the throne-theophany carries no formula-marked internal seam; the samekh recorded after 1:28 and the fresh 'he said to me' that opens oshb:Ezek.2.1 together mark the vision/commission seam on the FAR side of this unit; the onset evidence at oshb:Ezek.2.1 is weighed there.

current_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Isolating oshb:Ezek.1.1-1.3 as its own superscription unit, separate from the vision it introduces. Rejected because the vision proper (1:4-1:28) carries no independent onset device of its own - it simply continues the sentence the hand-of-YHWH clause opens - so cutting after 1:3 would manufacture a seam the bytes do not mark, and would still leave a 25-verse remainder with the same cap problem.
current_row.device_notes: Whole-chapter span (28 verses), well above the 7-10 typical density and above the 14-16 stretch cap for measured/listed blocks even though this is not such a block; disclosed under the E-02 cap posture and held low rather than forced into an unsupported internal cut. current_row.boundary_rationale: Onset: oshb:Ezek.2.1 וַיֹּ֖אמֶר אֵלָ֑י בֶּן אָדָם֙ עֲמֹ֣ד עַל רַגְלֶ֔יךָ ('he said to me, “Son of man, stand on your feet”') is the book's first 'he said to me' + 'son of man' pairing, following directly on the vision's close (samekh recorded after oshb:Ezek.1.28). The commissioning proper follows at 2:3, שׁוֹלֵ֨חַ אֲנִ֤י אֽוֹתְךָ֙ אֶל בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל (oshb:Ezek.2.3) ('I send you to the children of Israel'), and carries the book's first messenger formula at 2:4, כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֖ר אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהֹוִֽה (oshb:Ezek.2.4), embedded as reported speech rather than a fresh onset. The refrain כִּ֛י בֵּ֥ית מְרִ֖י הֵ֑מָּה (oshb:Ezek.2.5) ('for they are a rebellious house') recurs at 2:5 and 2:6 - the first two of the twelve book-wide occurrences, six of them clustered in this commission (2:5-3:27) and none in chapters 4-11 - texture for the unit, not yet its close. Close: the scroll-vision at 2:9, וְהִנֵּה יָ֖ד שְׁלוּחָ֣ה אֵלָ֑י (oshb:Ezek.2.9) ('behold, a hand stretched out to me'), through 2:10's inscription קִנִ֥ים וָהֶ֖גֶה וָהִֽי (oshb:Ezek.2.10) ('lamentations, mourning, and woe'), with the samekh recorded after 2:10. The scroll's eating (3:1-3) continues the same scene across the chapter break and is not cut here.

current_row.boundary_rationale: Onset: 3:12 וַתִּשָּׂאֵ֣נִי ר֔וּחַ (oshb:Ezek.3.12) ('then the Spirit lifted me up') begins the return-transport away from the plain-vision back to the exiles, distinct in texture from the preceding commissioning speech (no address, no imperative - narrated action). 3:14 carries the hand-of-YHWH construct, וְיַד יְהוָ֥ה עָלַ֖י חָזָֽקָה (oshb:Ezek.3.14) ('the hand of YHWH was strong upon me'); it is weighed and NOT read as a fresh vision onset here, in contrast to 1:3 and 3:22 - it sits inside a single continuous journey (lifted up → went in bitterness → came to Tel-abib) with no scene change around it, so it is disclosed as transit texture rather than a hard seam. Close: 3:15, וָאֵשֵׁ֥ב שָׁ֛ם שִׁבְעַ֥ת יָמִ֖ים מַשְׁמִ֥ים בְּתוֹכָֽם (oshb:Ezek.3.15) ('I sat there overwhelmed among them seven days'); no parashah mark is recorded at 3:15, which is not read as counterevidence against the seam. The gap this closes is temporal, not formulaic: 3:16 reopens on 'at the end of seven days' with its own strict word-event.

A 2mp recognition-family variant closes mid-unit at 7:9, וִֽידַעְתֶּ֕ם כִּ֛י אֲנִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה מַכֶּֽה (oshb:Ezek.7.9) ('then you will know that I, Yahweh, strike'); it was weighed as a candidate unit seam and set aside because no formula onset - no messenger formula, word-event or set-your-face - reopens at 7:10, which continues instead with unmarked poetic doom-announcement, הִנֵּ֥ה הַיּ֖וֹם הִנֵּ֣ה בָאָ֑ה (oshb:Ezek.7.10) ('behold, the day! behold, it comes!'). The WEB's own paragraphing marks further breaks at 7:10, 7:15 and 7:23 (the latter opening “make chains…”, web:Ezek.7.23); these are tier-4 and are disclosed as texture only, never as boundary evidence (E-23) - none coincides with a word-event, messenger formula, or set-your-face reopening the address. Close: 7:27, וְיָדְע֖וּ כִּֽי אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה (oshb:Ezek.7.27) ('then they will know that I am Yahweh'), the strict recognition formula, with a pe recorded after it; this is both the part's final unit and P2's close, with 8:1's dateline standing as the next hard seam outside this part.
